terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation, transitive; in the passive, to grow less
terms.gloss: make less, lessen; in the passive, decrease
evidence: Cic. Off. 1.123: senibus autem labōrēs corporis minuendī
terms.comment: Transitive: to make less (see make smaller); the passive is the everyday “to go down, grow less”.

evidence: Hor. C. 4.7.3: dēcrēscentia rīpās flūmina praetereunt
Cic. Div. 2.33: ostreae cum lūnā pariter crēscunt pariterque dēcrēscunt (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of what grows less of itself: rivers going down, the waning moon (dēcrēscente lūnā, Col. 12.47.2), a fever; the opposite of crēscō.

evidence: Caes. B.G. 1.53.6: neque dē tantā voluptāte et grātulātiōne quicquam fortūna dēminuerat (Lewis & Short)
Tac. Agr. 9.4: aut sevēritās amōrem dēminuit
terms.comment: To make less by taking something away (dē): with dē or ex and the ablative, to take away from.

evidence: Cic. Tusc. 1, 28: accrētiō et dēminūtiō lūminis (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The noun, in good prose (Lewis & Short); a decrease in revenue, in numbers, in rank.

phrases.latin: at memoria minuitur. crēdō, nisi eam exerceās
phrases.english: “But memory fades.” — I suppose so, unless you exercise it

phrases.latin: mūtat terra vicēs et dēcrēscentia rīpās flūmina praetereunt
phrases.english: the earth goes through its changes, and the rivers, going down, flow past within their banks

phrases.latin: nec illī, quod est rārissimum, aut facilitās auctōritātem aut sevēritās amōrem dēminuit
phrases.english: in him, the rarest thing, neither his easiness lessened his authority nor his strictness affection
